blocks.text: Refrigerator is a device which maintains the temperature of a body below that of its surrounding. It operates in a cyclic process but in reverse as that of the heat engine as shown in Fig.6.10. A refrigerator absorbs heat from a cold reservoir and gives it off to a hot reservoir. This shows that in a refrigerator, the work is done on the system while in a heat engine work is done by the system.

blocks.alt: A red bar labelled Higher temperature surroundings at the top and an orange bar labelled Low temperature compartment at the bottom, joined by a grey band through a grey circle labelled Refrigerator. Below the circle an up arrow QC, Heat in; above it an up arrow QH, Heat out. From the right an arrow labelled work points into the refrigerator: W.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.10: A refrigerator transfers heat from a low-temperature compartment to higher-temperature surroundings with the help of external work. It is a heat engine operating in reverse order (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.10).

blocks.text: A refrigerator works on the basis of Clausius statement of second law of thermodynamics, i.e., a heat engine is operating in reverse. Heat Q_C is drawn from Low Temperature Reservoir (LTR) by compressor and is thrown into High Temperature Reservoir (HTR) with the help of external work done. The heat rejected to HTR (Q_H) is given by

blocks.latex: Q_C + W = Q_H \qquad \text{or} \qquad W = Q_H - Q_C
blocks.text_alt: Q_C + W = Q_H   or   W = Q_H − Q_C

blocks.text: The main purpose of refrigerator is to extract as much heat Q_C as possible from LTR with the expenditure of as little work W as possible.
